newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premiums steady to lower, molasses weak.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premiums steady to lower, molasses weak.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums were steady to easier as weak fundamentals countered news of buying, trade sources said on Monday.
News of an Iranian purchase of three cargoes and talk of further buying by Indonesia for shipment next year barely moved the market, they told Reuters.

"As fundamentals remain weak, perhaps buyers sit out to wait for prices to drop further before entering the market again," one trader said, adding that Thai sugar was sold out until the end of the year.
January/March delivery was quoted at 0.80/0.85 cents a pound on an FOB basis over New York futures, barely changed from last week, traders said.
March/May delivery was bid at 0.70-0.75 cents over New York March compared with 0.75-0.80 last week, while May/July was quoted at around 0.65/0.75.
Another trader said he did not expect the bearish trend to be curbed unless there was a crop failure among major producing countries or a substantial rise in demand, which was unlikely.
"The 1997 export volume might not change much from this year, but the value is likely to decline," he said.
"High stocks and good crops are a bad combination. But in Asia, let's hope demand will continue to be bullish," he added.
But data for the first nine months of this year indicated Thailand's exports were still strong.

According to figures from commerce ministry and independent surveyors, Thai sugar exports rose 21 percent in the first nine months of 1996 to 4.26 million tonnes, against 3.52 million in the same period last year.
Thai molasses markets were quiet as prices continued to be battered by weak demand and exports from India.
Molasses prices plunged to around $40-50 per tonne FOB Bangkok from $124 in during June-July.
"The prices dropped sharply following the release of India's projection for molasses exports this year, which is way above a million tonne," said one molasses trader.
He added that Indian molasses was quoted around $41.

"The prices were so attractive that some of our traditional clients bleached contracts," another trader said, adding that Thailand's major buyers of mollasses included South Korea, Taiwan and Indonesia.
Thailand is expected to export around 970,000 tonnes of molasses this year compared with 1.08 million a year earlier.

At Thai ports, there was only one new declaration. E.D.& F Man bought 1,200 tonnes of white sugar for Indonesia. The vessel, Orient Express I, was scheduled to arrive for loading on November 8, industry sources said.
Bang Po had left Thai port with 2,3000 tonnes of white sugar for Indonesia. Xin An Jiang was scheduled to leave on November 7, also to Indonesia, with 13,100 tonnes of white sugar.
Kerry was said to be the buyer.
